items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I mean with the ballet or Alvin Ailey, they do a lot of things with jazz.

ctx.x: Yeah, oh man, suave, elegant, and a showman. Even that was a part of the show. And these guys were top musicians, I mean the best. But they never lost sight of that audience.

They brought something, and there was no dignity lost, because who could have more dignity than Duke Ellington? So musicians, you’re always going to have some people that are more serious and that’s good too. I mean there’s a place for — jazz is so big and so wide a range of feelings, you can have everything. Just know what’s what. And there are times when there are concert situations, and there should be times there are dance situations. And I don’t mean swing dancing, I mean with the ballet or Alvin Ailey, they…
I will quote your last interview. You said: “everything in balance.”
